hero.label: Neovanguard OS features
hero.title:
Features and
tools
hero.lead: Neovanguard brings together identity, payment and security tools in packages managed by pacman. The services run on your own machine.

layers.title: Nostr identity
layers.text: The installer can create the local account from a Nostr key, encrypted with a password using NIP-49. An encrypted vault stores the profile and settings so they can be restored on another installation.
items: local account with a Nostr key

layers.title: Bitcoin and Lightning
layers.text: Includes Bitcoin Core to run a full node, Core Lightning for payment channels and Sparrow for managing wallets and UTXOs. It also provides Elements for Liquid and Cashu tools.

layers.title: System security
layers.text: The default configuration keeps logs in RAM, applies noexec to /dev/shm and /var/tmp and uses restrictive nftables rules. Processes that handle keys use hardened_malloc.

layers.title: Vault mode
layers.text: A session available from the boot menu for signing operations. The wallet uses a directory in RAM, discarded at shutdown, with tools to isolate the network and sign PSBTs.

commands.title: neo-* commands
commands.lead: The neo-* commands help you manage nodes, wallets, networking and security. Run --help to see the options of each command. Some examples are listed below.

list.neo-status: Shows the state of the node, Lightning, relay, network and memory.
list.neo-zap: Sends sats over Lightning to an npub, address or invoice.
list.neo-ln: Checks the state and liquidity of Lightning channels.
list.neo-mempool: Checks fees and the state of the local mempool.
list.neo-sign: Signs a PSBT in an isolated environment.
list.neo-vault: Opens a wallet in a directory in RAM.
list.neo-shamir: Splits and rebuilds the seed with secret sharing.
list.neo-paper: Generates a template for a physical seed backup.
list.neo-qr: Transfers data between machines by QR code.
list.neo-airgap: Disables networking at the kernel level.
list.neo-killswitch: Blocks traffic outside the configured tunnel.
list.neo-tor: Sets up traffic routing through Tor.
list.neo-mac: Randomizes the MAC address of network interfaces.
list.neo-screenguard: Blocks screenshots while a seed is displayed.
list.neo-entropy: Checks the entropy available on the system.
list.neo-integrity: Verifies the integrity of installed binaries.
list.neo-relays: Measures relay latency and sorts the list.
list.neo-mesh: Finds Neovanguard machines on the network and exchanges notes.
list.neo-nuke: Runs the emergency RAM wipe and powers off the machine.

commands.more: The remaining commands cover power, network and memory management and session data cleanup.

desktop.title: Plasma, with the Birfree theme
desktop.text1: KDE Plasma is the default desktop environment, configured through the KDE settings application. The Birfree theme brings together Neovanguard's colors, icons and boot screen.
desktop.text2: Other desktop environments can be installed with pacman -S, using the packages available for Arch Linux.

verify.title: Verifying the image
verify.lead: Before writing the ISO, verify the SHA-256 checksum and the GPG signature. The examples below use the Live image; for Install, use the matching files.
verify.step1Text: The checksum detects differences between the downloaded file and the published value. It does not prove where the image came from.
verify.step1Result: The expected result is the file name followed by OK. That confirms integrity; check the signature as well.
verify.step2Text: The signature ties the image to the release key. To verify it, the matching public key must be imported into GPG.
verify.step2Result: Check the full fingerprint of the key used for the signature. The expected value is:

hero.label: Install Neovanguard OS
hero.title: Installation
hero.lead: Use the NVG Install image to install the system without internet. After booting from the USB drive, open the installer in the terminal. The Live image is for trying the system and does not include the installer.

prepare.title: Before you start
prepare.lead: Check the image availability on the download page and back up the files you want to keep. The default installation erases the chosen disk. The installer reports the required space before continuing.

cards.title: Check the image
cards.text: Verify the SHA-256 checksum and the GPG signature by following the instructions on the images page.

cards.title: Write it to the USB drive
cards.text: Use a tool that supports hybrid ISO images, such as dd, Ventoy, GNOME's USB image writer or Etcher. Do not extract the ISO.

cards.title: Boot from the USB drive
cards.text: Select the USB drive in the computer's boot menu. Disable Secure Boot on UEFI systems, since the images do not have a compatible signature yet.

launch.title: Open the installer
launch.result: The expected result is the installer's start screen in the terminal. If the command is not found, make sure you booted from the Install image.

flow.title: Basic offline installation
flow.lead: The system included on the media is copied to the disk. Networking is optional and lets you bring your Nostr identity. Before writing, the review step shows the chosen disk and the changes. The summary below groups the decisions; the number of screens depends on the media and on the recovered profile.

hero.label: About Neovanguard OS
hero.title:
About
Neovanguard OS
hero.lead: An Arch Linux-based distribution for running Bitcoin, Lightning and Nostr. It integrates command-line tools, key-based identity and local services into the KDE Plasma desktop.

goal.title: Running local services
goal.text1: The project brings together the components needed to manage nodes, wallets and relays on your own computer. The Nostr integration lets you use a key as your identity and restore settings across installations.
goal.text2: The installer, the settings vault and the neo-* commands support that use. The components are distributed as packages for Arch Linux.

team.title: Company and product, each with its own name
team.text: Neovanguard is the company. Neovanguard OS is the open source product it develops. Mizael Ribeiro, cofounder and CEO, leads product and development. João Antônio Rodrigues, cofounder and COO, leads operations, quality and security.

scope.title: Requirements and limitations
scope.lead: Consider the knowledge required, the limits of privacy and the responsibility for your keys before installing.

cards.title: Linux knowledge
cards.text: Managing nodes, relays and wallets requires familiarity with Linux, the terminal and networking. The project is aimed at people who intend to operate these services.

cards.title: Privacy limits
cards.text: Tor, blocking traffic outside the tunnel, MAC randomization and logs in RAM are privacy tools. Using them does not guarantee anonymity.

cards.title: License and warranty
cards.text: The project declares the GPL-3.0 license, without warranty. Development remains in a private repository; the public guides and notes describe the current state, without announcing available ISOs.

cards.title: Key custody
cards.text: The project keeps no copies of your keys and offers no identity recovery. It is up to the user to keep the Nostr key and its backups safe.

development.title: Code and tests
development.text1: Fixes include regression tests for the defects identified. These tests check the failure on the affected version and the result after the fix.
development.text2: Build checks aim to catch problems before installation, especially in the steps that change the disk.

sections.title: What we collect
items: Audience measurement: anonymous browsing statistics, without individual identification cookies.
Forms: the website has no forms for submitting a name, email address or phone number.
Language preference: the language chosen in the switcher is saved only in your browser and is not sent to the server.

sections.title: The package repository
sections.text: The /repo address distributes signed packages without requiring a login or an installation identifier. Accessing the files may generate hosting logs, as with other web services.

sections.title: Operating system
sections.text: Neovanguard OS does not send telemetry. By default, system logs stay in RAM and are discarded at shutdown. The relays used by the Nostr identity are chosen by the user, independently of this website.

sections.title: Use of data
items: We do not sell or share your data with third parties for marketing.
We do not send bulk email: you only receive a reply to what you asked.

sections.title: Your rights (LGPD)
sections.text: You can request access to, correction of or deletion of your data at any time through our contact channel. We respond within the legal deadline.

sections.title: Retention
sections.text: Contact messages are kept only for as long as needed for support and legal obligations.

sections.title: Content
sections.text: The texts, brand and visual material on this website belong to Neovanguard and may not be reproduced without permission.

sections.title: Information about the system
sections.text: The information on this website describes Neovanguard OS. See the repository for the source code, the system license and the distribution conditions.

sections.title: Availability

sections.title: Contact

detail.title: Neovanguard OS 1.2.1 in preparation
detail.intro: The source changelog records version 1.2.1 in preparation, authorized on September 12, 2026. The Live and Install ISOs are not publicly available. There is no confirmed publication date.
changed: Firewall state, VPN DNS and endpoint checks, and Shamir set validation.
Packaging and build checks, with explicit failure reporting.
detail.validationTitle: Validation and publication are separate steps
detail.validation1: The notes record local checks. That does not prove a complete release build, boot on hardware, offline installation or an independent cryptographic review. Packages only reach installations after being published to the configured update repository.
detail.validation2: The documented CI keeps checksums temporarily and does not distribute ISOs. A checksum is not an image download.
